desert_p13_001.speaker: narrator
desert_p13_001.text: By morning the expedition had found a palace, lost two men, and returned with a tank full of poisoned water. None of these reports agreed with the others, but all three had reached the bun seller before Yue reached his counter. He asked which version she preferred. She said she preferred breakfast. He wrapped two hot buns and leaned closer, hoping that generosity might improve her answer. Through the steam she explained that both guides were alive, the tank held ordinary travelling water, and the largest building they had seen was a weighing hall.

desert_p13_002.speaker: narrator
desert_p13_002.text: He looked disappointed by the hall and distinctly relieved by the guides. The first report deadline fell that afternoon. Han had obtained a table in the cooperative receiving room, where a blue fly walked across the clean inkwell lid with complete ownership. Gao arranged the exterior drawings in the order a driver would need them. Du brought the copied window columns in a separate folder. Their returning equipment stood in the yard under the keeper's charge; the issued clothes could wait until they were dry.

desert_p13_003.speaker: narrator
desert_p13_003.text: Yue laid the village's requests beside the tank incident account and found that there was almost no room left for the picturesque building that had already become a palace in town.

desert_p13_004.speaker: gao_ru
desert_p13_004.text: Put the loading warning on top. People who only read one sheet should meet that first. The bird mark can wait; the north window can wait; even the water sample table can wait beneath the source description. No, Du, I am not throwing away your columns. I want the first driver who takes this bundle to know which ground will carry his cart before he wonders who put a crooked bird on a page. You can have as many following pages as you need, provided you leave me one clear beginning.

desert_p13_005.speaker: narrator
desert_p13_005.text: Du complied more quickly than Yue expected. Then he changed the first sheet's title from Survey Result to Present Route Warning and gave it back. Gao read the new title twice, accepted it, and drew a heavy line beneath the restriction. The fly returned to the inkwell. Yue placed a spare cup over it, which improved the proceedings immediately. Han arrived carrying his daughter's enormous-flowered cart drawing under the repair invoices. He had mistaken one folded page for another in the rush. Gao said the flower canopy would make the loading warning easier to remember.

desert_p13_006.speaker: narrator
desert_p13_006.text: Han hid the drawing inside his coat before she could use it. The cooperative clerk wanted the report divided into three matters: route condition, water custody, and expenses. The village representatives' crop request did not fit comfortably in any of them. He suggested attaching it to expenses, then noticed Han watching him and changed the suggestion to a separate referred concern. Yue wrote the receiving date on both copies while the clerk located the seal. The woman from the drying yard would come on the next market wagon. Until then, the request was no substitute for her own account.

desert_p13_007.speaker: narrator
desert_p13_007.text: It was also no longer something an office could say it had never received. Han kept the sealed duplicate in sight. The cooperative's chair was an elderly freight broker with two narrow spectacles, one for the page and one for the room. She put on the page pair to examine the collar loss. Her first question was whether the travelling reserve had been counted separately from the routine stock. Han showed the entries, including the necessary five litres drawn on the last day.

desert_p13_008.speaker: narrator
desert_p13_008.text: She removed the spectacles and asked why the protected thread had not simply been omitted from the report. The silence became uncomfortable. Han said because it had been cut. She nodded, looking almost pleased, and ordered the repair investigation to continue without wage deductions until its findings were available.

desert_p13_009.speaker: han_xun
desert_p13_009.text: I want the tank examined before somebody decides the driver is the cheapest explanation. He stopped the pair straight, held the brake and gave the farrier room. We have his account and the other driver's account. The bent collar is in the workshop now. If it shows an inspection failure, the inspection belongs in the record. If it shows impact damage without a defect we could have seen, that belongs there too. My crew do not become a reserve fund merely because the water reserve ran short. I have already paid them under the terms I hired them on.

desert_p13_010.speaker: narrator
desert_p13_010.text: The chair looked at the repair invoice and asked whether he could afford to sound so firm. Han's hand moved toward the coat pocket containing his daughter's drawing. He left it there. He said he could afford the agreed wages, which was the immediate question. The chair made a small mark on the account margin. Yue saw how different his answer was from the smiling assurance he gave customers. It had room in it for bills he did not intend to show the room. The chair allowed the carrying surcharge but asked for the cask keeper's cancelled receipt.

desert_p13_011.speaker: narrator
desert_p13_011.text: Gao produced the receipt, stained at one corner with harmless kettle smoke. The water officer came from a different room and disliked being summoned into a freight discussion. He read Bao's controls and batch entries, then asked whether the cooperative intended to sell the stored source as a public station. Gao said no such opening had been agreed. The caretaker's maintenance and the expedition's limited tested draw were separate facts. The officer asked to see the source sketch. When he saw the old settling pocket, his annoyance gave way to interest. He knew the waterhouse form.

desert_p13_012.speaker: narrator
desert_p13_012.text: An aunt of his had operated one inland before the upper trade shifted. He began asking useful questions about its roof and isolated outlet.

desert_p13_013.speaker: bao_sun
desert_p13_013.text: We screened the water drawn on that day with our field kit and controls, then filtered and boiled it because the source was a stored rain supply within the applicable limits. The record gives the actual cooled quantity. It does not promise a future yield or certify whatever might flow through the nearby channel tomorrow. The caretaker can tell you about her maintenance. A source officer can inspect what she tells you.

desert_p13_014.speaker: bao_sun
desert_p13_014.text: Meanwhile, there are two injured guides in town who need your clinic supply to remain ordinary, reliable and available without being dragged into a rumour about a poisoned palace.

desert_p13_015.speaker: narrator
desert_p13_015.text: The officer's expression sharpened at the word poisoned. He said he had heard the rumour himself. Bao opened her clinic transfer notes but kept the patients' private details covered. There was no exposure diagnosis tying their injuries to the stored source; the rescue had preceded the expedition's draw. The officer wrote a short factual notice for the municipal desk and asked Bao to review the medical sentence before he sealed it. She shortened it. He accepted the change without making a speech about it. Yue thought of the bun seller.

desert_p13_016.speaker: narrator
desert_p13_016.text: A notice might reach him too late to be interesting, but it would give the next worried parent somewhere to ask. By noon the meeting had run out of clean cups and everyone had developed an opinion about the room's window. Du wanted it open for light; the clerk wanted it closed against dust; the chair wanted whoever had moved her spectacles to confess. Yue found them beneath the cask receipt. The chair put them on her head and went on reading.

desert_p13_017.speaker: narrator
desert_p13_017.text: A carrier representative asked whether the northern exchange could be restored cheaply, given that the glass case still existed. Gao replied that a surviving case carried almost no useful information about a buried roof's strength. The representative tapped the case drawing as if it had promised him otherwise.

desert_p13_018.speaker: du_she
desert_p13_018.text: My old map is one of the reasons you expected that ground to be useful. I compressed the station's later restrictions into an appendix most buyers did not carry. I believed the main road would remain in seasonal use. That was a judgement, and it aged badly. The copied northern record gives us a place to look for the fuller sequence. I will publish a dated correction to the existing sheets and withdraw the plain freight symbol at the lower exchange. You may be angry with me for that.

desert_p13_019.speaker: du_she
desert_p13_019.text: You should still take the correction before you send another loaded cart.

desert_p13_020.speaker: narrator
desert_p13_020.text: A man near the door accused him of protecting his better customers. Du asked which instruction the man meant. The man waved a private printed route card dated three months earlier. Its publisher was a rival office that had copied Du's older exchange symbol, added a shorter approach, and retained only a little footnote about light traffic. Du did not enjoy admitting that the familiar symbol was his. The rival's additions did not erase his own omission. Gao spread the old sheet, the newer card and the field sketch side by side.

desert_p13_021.speaker: narrator
desert_p13_021.text: Their different dates became visible without anyone needing to be declared the sole author of the bad road. The rival card had a red corner mark showing a subscription class. Han recognized the mark from his own purchase cabinet. He had bought a set for a grain client and recommended the neat folding cover. The memory put colour into his face. The carrier representative asked how many clients had received them. Han named the number he could confirm from invoices and said he would check for resales. The chair ordered a distribution enquiry.

desert_p13_022.speaker: narrator
desert_p13_022.text: Yue watched the cooperative clerk turn to a fresh sheet. The room's palace had dwindled into paper, but the paper could still send real wheels toward a real break.

desert_p13_023.speaker: gao_ru
desert_p13_023.text: I need one current warning circulated through both offices today. Use the route identifiers and the exterior sketch; do not wait for the argument over who pays for the replacement printing. The lower apron stays barred to loaded traffic. The public ridge remains the observed alternative for carts within its present conditions. Any proposed inspection has to coordinate with the people below the drain. I will sign the field observations. Du can sign the source correction. Han can attach the customer list he actually knows.

desert_p13_024.speaker: gao_ru
desert_p13_024.text: The three signatures mean three kinds of knowledge; do not print them as three votes certifying the whole valley.

desert_p13_025.speaker: narrator
desert_p13_025.text: They left the room in the heat of early afternoon. The rival's representative had arrived too late to speak and was standing on the steps with a face like a tightly folded receipt. He wore a fine grey hat whose brim had survived the dust better than anything on the expedition. Du recognized him and said his name quietly, but Yue heard only the tone. The man asked to discuss the correction privately. Du agreed to an appointment the following morning, with Gao present for the route facts.

desert_p13_026.speaker: narrator
desert_p13_026.text: The man's glance passed over her field case and lingered on the frayed shoulder strap. He did not look pleased. At the workshop the second cart stood over a shallow inspection pit. Its tank had been drained under the keeper's record before removal, and the remaining travelling stock transferred to the yard's clean return vessel by measured entries. The damaged collar lay on a white board beside an older spare. A smith pointed to a dark line within the fracture. The outside face alone would not have shown it; the mounting had to be loosened to expose that region.

desert_p13_027.speaker: narrator
desert_p13_027.text: He wanted the purchase record and the last full service note before giving a cause. Han had expected relief from the examination. Instead he got another precise unanswered question. The driver arrived with his daughter's wooden bird under one arm. He had brought it to a carpenter across the lane for a nick in its tail. Seeing Han, he began to explain why he was not at the cooperative. Han said he was off the road and free to repair a bird. The smith invited both men to inspect the collar.

desert_p13_028.speaker: narrator
desert_p13_028.text: The driver stared at the inner crack, then asked whether he should have heard it developing. The smith said not reliably from the seat. He demonstrated how the brace had hidden the sound with a dull tap. The driver stood straighter, though he did not yet smile. Gao checked the tank frame drawing against the broken mounting while Yue held the lamp. It was a workshop lamp, loaned by the smith for the examination, and Yue kept it outside the oil tray. The farrier arrived carrying his repair box and described how the temporary piece had seated.

desert_p13_029.speaker: narrator
desert_p13_029.text: The smith wanted to retain that piece for comparison, so they wrote its borrowed custody and return date before the farrier left. A junior worker asked Yue whether the northern ruins had a floor of black glass. She answered that the glass they saw was a cabinet front. He lost interest in the cabinet and immediately asked whether it could be sold. On the way back, Gao bought paper from a stationer who stocked it beside candle wicks. Her purse came from the field allowance, nearly depleted now; she selected the coarser batch. Yue offered to contribute from her wages.

desert_p13_030.speaker: narrator
desert_p13_030.text: Gao considered, then refused because the new copies were part of her commissioned work. Yue bought her own fresh pages anyway. Her blank notebook was no longer blank, and several sheets had become dense with hurried figures. The stationer wrapped both purchases in one sheet to save them a little. Outside, Gao separated the bundles carefully. Different people had bought them for different days ahead. Tuo had not attended the long hearing. Bao found her at home beneath a vine that looked too thin to make so much shade.

desert_p13_031.speaker: narrator
desert_p13_031.text: A neighbour had brought broth and stayed to criticize every object in the small courtyard. Tuo introduced Yue as the person who had held a cover over a man's head until he stopped a tank leaking. The neighbour approved of that, then asked why Lin had not simply closed the tank with cultivation. Tuo said that unknown metal did not become familiar because a cultivator was nearby. Yue was grateful for the answer and even more grateful when Bao asked the neighbour to move the stool out of the examination space.

desert_p13_032.speaker: narrator
desert_p13_032.text: The ankle was less swollen, its colour moving through the ugly yellow of repair. Bao compared the range with her previous notes and examined the tender side again. Tuo could make short supported movements without sharp pain, but the uneven ruin approach had to wait for another check. She accepted this grudgingly, then asked how many people at the cooperative had pretended they knew the old roads. Yue said fewer after the maps were laid out. Tuo laughed and demanded the full account, especially the rival's grey hat.

desert_p13_033.speaker: narrator
desert_p13_033.text: Bao allowed the conversation while she worked, provided Tuo stopped turning her foot to illustrate every point.

desert_p13_034.speaker: tuo_yin
desert_p13_034.text: Du always despised those corner marks. He said a map ought to fold the same way in every hand. Then he began selling three paper weights, two covers and a private appendix. He can make a principle fit inside a purse if he has enough time. Still, I am glad he stood up today. It is harder to correct your own old mark when somebody else has made money with it. Tell him I said that, but leave out the glad part if he has become unbearable. No, leave it in.

desert_p13_035.speaker: tuo_yin
desert_p13_035.text: I have spent too long making him guess what I meant.

desert_p13_036.speaker: narrator
desert_p13_036.text: The neighbour returned with a plate of preserved pears and looked offended to find the examination complete. She had hoped to advise Bao. Instead she advised Yue about boot soles and scolded Tuo for owning a chair that tilted toward the injured foot. Tuo invited her to repair it. The neighbour examined the joint, announced that her nephew had a better clamp, and left at once to fetch him. The courtyard became quiet. Bao packed her bag. Tuo looked at the empty gate and said that every injury in this street eventually became three people's carpentry.

desert_p13_037.speaker: narrator
desert_p13_037.text: Yue ate a pear and felt the road settle a little farther behind her. That evening Han's household ate beside an open window looking onto a brick wall. The view was not grand, but it belonged to people who had planted a basil pot on the sill. His mother coughed once and accepted the cup his daughter brought without accepting the daughter's advice about when to drink it. Han had invited Yue and Gao to the meal because his family wanted to meet the expedition, and because he did not know how to describe it alone.

desert_p13_038.speaker: narrator
desert_p13_038.text: The soup contained more vegetables than their camp meals had seen in several days. Yue caught herself studying the water in her bowl before she began to eat.

desert_p13_039.speaker: han_xun
desert_p13_039.text: My daughter says I should put the flower cart into our signboard. She thinks people would hire a man who transported spring. My mother thinks they would hire a man who admitted when a wheel needed grease. You have heard both proposals now. I would value a professional judgement before they begin fighting over the brush. Gao, do not recommend that I become a gardener. We tried a second basil pot last year and it died in a week. That was not a supply failure; I had agreed to water it and kept assuming somebody else already had.

desert_p13_040.speaker: narrator
desert_p13_040.text: Gao voted for a small flower beside a properly greased wheel. Han's daughter declared this cowardly compromise and drew it anyway on the back of an old bill. His mother asked whether the guide with the broken leg had a mother nearby. Bao's account had reached Han's family only as a safe return; he explained the blue shawl and the continuing treatment. The older woman nodded and told him to send pears, not advice. When he asked how many, she counted with her fingers against the table. Yue watched him accept an instruction without negotiating it.

desert_p13_041.speaker: narrator
desert_p13_041.text: In this room, he could be somebody's son. Du did not come to dinner. He spent the evening above his office, taking old editions from a shelf that had begun to bow under their accumulated certainty. His apprentice brought him tea and found him comparing two captions that differed by a single word. Seasonal had vanished between them. He could remember wanting room for a clearer ferry drawing on that edition. The memory was painfully ordinary. He wrote the date on a correction slip and placed the slip inside both copies.

desert_p13_042.speaker: narrator
desert_p13_042.text: When the apprentice asked how far back they were going to look, he said far enough to stop guessing, and sent her home before the work became her unpaid night. Yue returned to her rented room carrying a little soup Han's mother had insisted on packing. The bowl was the household's, to be brought back tomorrow; she wrote its owner inside the paper wrapper because borrowed things had a way of acquiring forgetful homes. The shopkeeper's daughter had left the repaired cloak folded by the door. Yue touched the new seam and found it straighter than her own stitches.

desert_p13_043.speaker: narrator
desert_p13_043.text: In the courtyard below, rainwater from an earlier shower had collected in a pot for the flowers. Nobody was counting it as travelling stock. She lay down and listened to a cart pass along the lane without feeling obliged to follow it. The next morning a printer's runner delivered the first corrected warning while Yue was returning the soup bowl. The sheet was smaller than Gao had requested because the press had used a remnant batch. Its central restriction remained legible; the lower footnote did not.

desert_p13_044.speaker: narrator
desert_p13_044.text: Han held it at arm's length, frowned, and sent the runner back with payment for a proper replacement. The runner asked whether the flawed sheets should be burned. Gao, arriving behind him, said they could serve as proofs with the defect marked plainly across them. The boy was pleased to carry back something other than blame. His basket contained enough bad paper already. On the fresh proof, the rival office's grey corner had become a black date box. Du's source correction occupied the bottom third; Gao's observed route filled the top.

desert_p13_045.speaker: narrator
desert_p13_045.text: Han read the warning aloud while his daughter listened from the stairs. She interrupted to ask whether a tired driver would understand apron as a piece of clothing. Gao looked at the word, then changed it to buried work roof and kept the technical term in brackets below. Du objected for half a breath and then crossed out his own objection. The girl leaned over the rail to watch the next mark. At last there was a professional use for her questions. The rival map office occupied the lower room of a spice merchant's house.

desert_p13_046.speaker: narrator
desert_p13_046.text: Pepper hung in the air strongly enough to make Du sneeze before anyone greeted him. Its representative had taken off the grey hat and placed it beneath the table, perhaps remembering Gao's glance. He offered chairs, tea and an explanation of the private card's shorter approach. A travelling correspondent had described the turning ground as restored. The office possessed his letter, but had never obtained a structural inspection. Gao asked to read the letter. The man produced it from a locked drawer and set it between them with the care usually given to a much stronger defence.

desert_p13_047.speaker: narrator
desert_p13_047.text: The correspondent had seen empty handcarts cross the surface in dry weather. He had written those limits in his account. The printed card retained dry weather and lost empty. The representative's thumb rested on the omitted word. Du said nothing while Gao compared the dates. The mistake had occurred between the letter and the card, within this room's own production. The man asked whether correcting it publicly would expose them to every carrier's compensation claim. Du replied that leaving it uncorrected would expose the next carrier to the ground. The man removed his thumb and asked for Gao's recommended wording.

desert_p13_048.speaker: gao_ru
desert_p13_048.text: Use the observed restriction and say that the former card overstated the load. Keep the correspondent's letter in your file. He described what he actually saw; the printed instruction said more. If you want an inspection, contribute to one with the collective and route authority. An inspection is work we can arrange. A sentence declaring the building sound is something I cannot sell you, however convenient it would be to have it by noon. I am willing to sign a present warning on your paper as well as Du's.

desert_p13_049.speaker: gao_ru
desert_p13_049.text: I will charge for the time it takes to prepare it, and you may put that cost in your printing account.

desert_p13_050.speaker: narrator
desert_p13_050.text: The representative listened as though this last offer had surprised him most. He had expected a demand to surrender the whole publication to Du. Instead she named a fee and held out a clean copy. He accepted the fee, then asked Du whether the newer road symbol could remain. Du examined it without his usual expression of ownership. He said the approach needed its proper origin and the loaded turning restriction beside it. The symbol itself was clear. The rival man looked down, uncomfortably pleased.

desert_p13_051.speaker: narrator
desert_p13_051.text: Yue, who had come to carry the field folder, realised she had been preparing to dislike him more simply than the room allowed. Outside, Du bought a small packet of pepper for Tuo. He said it was not an apology, merely something she liked in broth. Gao said he could take an apology and pepper in the same hand. He examined the packet, apparently considering this as a technical proposition. Then he admitted that Tuo had disliked his mother's pepper broth and preferred ginger. The merchant heard him from the doorway and exchanged the packet before Du could escape.

desert_p13_052.speaker: narrator
desert_p13_052.text: Yue carried the ginger while he carried the warning proofs. There was enough humiliation in both bundles to make him walk a little faster toward the guide's street. Tuo's neighbour had successfully repaired the chair and unsuccessfully persuaded Tuo to replace it. They found her seated on the finished joint with one heel above a cushion. Du put the ginger on the table. She looked at it, then at him, and said he had remembered eventually. He asked whether she was well enough to listen to a tiresome mapmaker.

desert_p13_053.speaker: narrator
desert_p13_053.text: She said she had been doing that for years while in perfect health. Yue and Gao went to the courtyard wall to examine the drying vine instead of hovering over the conversation. The vine had three leaves and still managed to create a place where people could pretend not to hear.

desert_p13_054.speaker: du_she
desert_p13_054.text: I came to your brother's inquiry with a sequence of dispatch dates because dates were what I knew how to carry. I should have asked what you needed before I laid them down. I cannot repair that meeting by being useful at this one. But I can stop pretending that knowing the sequence made me understand your winter. There is something else. The north records office taught me which changes disappeared when maps were made clean. I used that knowledge selectively.

desert_p13_055.speaker: du_she
desert_p13_055.text: You were right to be angry when I arrived with a sheet that had more room for a road than for what it had cost to keep the road open.

desert_p13_056.speaker: tuo_yin
desert_p13_056.text: I wanted you to say his name. Just once, before you told me which wagon had left first. I know the dates mattered. The compensation depended on them, and his wife used the money to keep the children at school. We were not too proud for that help. But you stood in my doorway as if the order of things was the whole thing. I have been angry enough to make that your only shape ever since. You are not his winter, Du. You were a man in the doorway who failed me for an hour.

desert_p13_057.speaker: tuo_yin
desert_p13_057.text: I can remember the hour without making it the rest of your life.

desert_p13_058.speaker: narrator
desert_p13_058.text: He did say the brother's name then, quietly enough that Yue did not take it for herself. Tuo put two cups on the table and poured the tea her neighbour had brought. The ginger lay between them like a ridiculous third guest. Gao climbed the courtyard wall's shallow step and cut a dead vine strand where Tuo directed her. The remaining leaves shifted into a cleaner pattern of light. Nobody announced reconciliation. When Du left, Tuo asked him to bring the corrected public route sheet next time, because she still wanted to see what he had done with the ridge.

desert_p13_059.speaker: narrator
desert_p13_059.text: He said he would come tomorrow with it. At the workshop, the second report was ready by late afternoon. The broken collar showed an old inner crack at a sharp tooling change, enlarged by the impact. The shop's service schedule had inspected the exposed brace and valve action but had not required the concealed face to be loosened at that interval. The smith could identify the hidden defect and the final fresh break. He could not date the first crack from the surface alone.

desert_p13_060.speaker: narrator
desert_p13_060.text: Han read the report, signed the tank's withdrawal from travel service, and ordered the comparable mountings on his other carts opened before their next hire. His returning driver was invited to witness the checks, on paid time. The driver accepted the invitation and asked whether his daughter could watch the carpenter finish the bird while he waited. Han said yes if the carpenter agreed. That small negotiation seemed to relieve him more than the smith's report had done. In the next bay, a mule belonging to another carrier objected loudly to having its shoe inspected.

desert_p13_061.speaker: narrator
desert_p13_061.text: The farrier answered it in a tone he normally reserved for obstinate customers. Yue stood outside the marked work space, smelling hot iron and wet leather. She could imagine the hidden line in the collar now without hearing water whenever she thought of it. The line had acquired a place in a repair. Gao's licensing office wanted a supplemental source statement. Her original application for the northern commission had relied partly on Du's edition; the office needed to know which observations had replaced that reliance.

desert_p13_062.speaker: narrator
desert_p13_062.text: She complained about the timing until Yue reminded her that the same information made the public warning stronger. Gao gave her a narrow look, then handed her the rough statement to read. It admitted the first map's limits and attached the field measurements. It did not pretend that Gao had recognized every problem before she saw it. Yue found one sentence in which the instrument's accuracy was offered as if it proved the building's capacity. Gao crossed it out herself.

desert_p13_063.speaker: gao_ru
desert_p13_063.text: I passed my survey examination by measuring things somebody else had prepared. A wall, a level, a distance with known reference marks. The examiners made me repeat the work when my figures drifted, and that was fair. This commission gave me people who remembered different beginnings and a road built out of somebody's old work. I still want the figures to be good. I also want to stop asking good figures to excuse a bad premise. It is infuriating to have the same argument printed in the licensing office's nicest hand. Let me be infuriated for a minute.

desert_p13_064.speaker: gao_ru
desert_p13_064.text: Then I will copy the statement properly.

desert_p13_065.speaker: narrator
desert_p13_065.text: Yue let her have the minute. They ate sesame cakes on the licensing steps while the clerk inside looked for another missing seal. A child tried to balance a twig on the head of a stone lion. His older sister told him the lion would sneeze if he succeeded. Gao laughed abruptly, the sound startling both children. She had been so tight with fatigue that her own amusement seemed to surprise her. Yue gave the boy a broken cake corner after his sister accepted the offer. The twig fell.

desert_p13_066.speaker: narrator
desert_p13_066.text: The lion continued to hold its professional expression, considerably more composed than the surveyor beside it. The village representatives arrived on the following market morning. Their wagon carried reed screens beneath a canvas sheet and two baskets of packed lunch. The woman wore her ordinary blue jacket, cleaned at the collar, and had wrapped the documents exactly as Du showed her. Han met them before the cooperative opened. He offered a room to wait in, but the mat maker preferred to leave the wagon where customers could see the screens.

desert_p13_067.speaker: narrator
desert_p13_067.text: By the time the receiving clerk unlocked the door, he had sold three mats. His companion watched the coins change hands, then asked Han whether an office appointment could be delayed by successful business. He said five minutes would not damage hers. The hearing moved to a room with enough benches for the collective and the drainage officer. The woman put her brother's field account down in her own voice. She did not say the ruined seedlings proved the whole claim; she said she wanted the officer to walk the ground while the boundary marks were still visible.

desert_p13_068.speaker: narrator
desert_p13_068.text: The officer agreed to a local inspection in two days, assigning a known deputy and leaving a written appointment at the village. The carter's request to reconsider the lower turning ground went into the same meeting but a separate work proposal. Nobody had to abandon one concern to be allowed the other. The mat maker opened a screen across two benches to show the carter why the ridge cost mattered. Goods had to be bundled more tightly for the longer journey; bent reed corners sold badly at market.

desert_p13_069.speaker: narrator
desert_p13_069.text: He put one damaged corner beside an intact one and asked the freight broker what her own buyers would pay. She inspected both without pretending ignorance. The grass village was neither an obstacle to commerce nor a perfect innocent living outside it. Its people wanted to sell screens and keep fields. The officer asked whether an inspection team could use the village's old storage shed on the return route. The woman said they could ask its present keeper, who had hens in it.

desert_p13_070.speaker: han_xun
desert_p13_070.text: If another survey is agreed, its costs cannot come out of the crop compensation before that claim is examined. My firm can contribute carts and a portion of the hire. The cooperative has customers who need a dependable northern route. The rival press now has customers who need an accurate account of the shorter one. Both can contribute to obtaining it. That does not buy them the collective's ground. I am willing to put my share in escrow with the receiving house, provided the inspection scope and the return provision are written before anyone loads a tank.

desert_p13_071.speaker: narrator
desert_p13_071.text: The chair asked how much he meant by a portion. Han named a sum smaller than Yue expected and looked embarrassed for exactly one breath. The sum was still substantial beside the last trip's remaining profit. The rival office's representative named another contribution, conditional on receiving the same publishable findings as other subscribers. Gao agreed to equal release of the public route facts. The village woman asked who would pay for a return visit if the first inspection could not answer everything. Nobody answered immediately. The chair wrote a second phase beneath the first and left its sum blank.

desert_p13_072.speaker: narrator
desert_p13_072.text: At least the blank had a place where everyone could see it. Du brought a folded letter from his old records office. The letter belonged to his retained correspondence, not the papers behind the northern glass. It referred to a Stone Channel traverse that had continued east of the lower exchange toward a seasonal relay valley. A small sketch showed two gates and a narrowing between rock shoulders. The exact relation between the named route and the quarry's new north cut still needed current observation. The drainage officer recognized one gate identifier from a surviving municipal file.

desert_p13_073.speaker: narrator
desert_p13_073.text: He asked Du for a copy and promised to locate the fuller record. Du kept the original dry in its sleeve and allowed the dated copying.

desert_p13_074.speaker: du_she
desert_p13_074.text: There was a relay store beyond that narrowing. It was old even when I worked north. I know its office designation, not its present roof. The old settlement was called Onion Hollow. There were seasonal households along the approach, and the work notes use their well as a level reference. If the diversion now follows that channel, they need to be found before the water is treated as an empty valley's problem. I can help read the identifiers. I do not know whether the road is still passable, whether the well is open, or which families remain.

desert_p13_075.speaker: du_she
desert_p13_075.text: Those are questions a current journey might answer.

desert_p13_076.speaker: narrator
desert_p13_076.text: The valley's name changed the meeting. The cooperative had treated the north cut as a drainage terminus; the officer now looked for a receiving district instead. Tuo, brought by a hired town chair after Bao approved the short transfer, remembered the narrowing from a winter journey many years earlier. She had crossed its outer track, never the relay store's interior. Her account fitted the two rock shoulders but not the letter's old approach turn. Gao drew the disagreement in two colours.

desert_p13_077.speaker: narrator
desert_p13_077.text: The proposed trip acquired a purpose beyond improving a map: establish where current diverted water went, which people occupied its path, and what could safely be inspected from the present ground. A market musician began playing in the street outside, directly beneath the hearing window. The chair sent the clerk to request a little distance. He returned with the musician, who thought she wanted to commission a song. The misunderstanding brought the only general laugh of the morning. The village woman laughed longest, then apologised for it and was told she need not.

desert_p13_078.speaker: narrator
desert_p13_078.text: Han bought the musician a bun and suggested the gate steps, where the echo was better. Yue watched the man leave with his flute held under his arm. Ordinary arrangements could sometimes be made without a seal, especially when somebody was willing to buy breakfast. The drainage officer's deputy arrived near the end with a rolled municipal trace. Its northern section was incomplete, but the first receiving gate and rock narrowing lay on it under the same identifiers as Du's letter. At the valley edge, a thin blue line ended at a notation for a community well.

desert_p13_079.speaker: narrator
desert_p13_079.text: The community name had been replaced by a district number in later editions. The deputy remembered a petition for lining repairs from that district the previous year. He had not handled it himself. He agreed to locate the petition rather than build a current village out of his memory. The roll made everyone lean forward, then made them sit back and wait. After the meeting, the woman representative asked Yue whether people in town always spoke so much before visiting a ditch. Yue said some people spoke more afterward.

desert_p13_080.speaker: narrator
desert_p13_080.text: The woman looked at the cooperative building, then down at her brother's remaining seed bag. She had wanted someone to admit that his field existed. Now there was a named visitor and a day. It was more than she had yesterday and less than the crop she needed. She bought a small jar of bean paste from the market and wrapped it among the papers. The mat maker had sold enough screens to pay their travel without help. They chose their own wagon home. Yue took the guide's mother her promised brief update, omitting the hearing's private arguments.

desert_p13_081.speaker: narrator
desert_p13_081.text: The younger woman's leg was supported for continuing treatment; she was awake and annoyed by a fly he could not reach. Her mother had already moved the water glass farther from the notebook. She asked whether the officials had remembered the warning card she had followed. Yue said its limited observations were now in the correction enquiry. The young woman closed his eyes. She did not want to become the face printed beside every unsafe map. Her mother said she would not, and looked at Yue until she agreed that her private story remained hers.

desert_p13_082.speaker: narrator
desert_p13_082.text: Bao found Yue in the clinic passage and handed her a packet of spent field-kit slips for the source file. The usable remainder remained in Bao's custody. Before another journey she would need fresh sets, sufficient medical supplies and a clearer forecast for the northern water source. She also wanted a stoneworker if anyone meant to approach the relay store. Yue asked whether she thought Tuo could go. Bao said the ankle's next examination would answer the walking question; wanting her expertise was not an examination. She would consider a limited route role only if the recovery supported it.

desert_p13_083.speaker: narrator
desert_p13_083.text: Yue carried the slips back to Gao without adding a hopeful yes. At dusk Du's apprentice laid the old and corrected editions along the office counter. She had found a caption in the earliest sheet that named the valley community rather than its later district number. The name did not match the ruin hunters' palace story. It sounded like an ordinary place where people might grow onions and mend roofs. Du checked it against his retained letter and marked the agreement, not the certainty of present occupation.

desert_p13_084.speaker: narrator
desert_p13_084.text: He asked the apprentice to add the community name as historical, with the district reference beside it. She asked whether that would clutter the clean road. He said yes, and for once sounded content with the clutter. Han walked home carrying the cooperative's proposed contribution schedule. His daughter met him at the door and asked whether he was leaving again. He said the next work could proceed without him on the road, if the hire was agreed. She looked relieved before she looked guilty. He touched the flower drawing now pinned beside the household shelf.

desert_p13_085.speaker: narrator
desert_p13_085.text: His mother needed an appointment at the clinic later in the week, and his accounts needed a person who knew which bills were real. He could help another journey happen from here. The decision cost him the pleasure of being indispensable at its front, a pleasure he had enjoyed more than he admitted.

desert_p13_086.speaker: han_xun
desert_p13_086.text: I will provide the carts, inspect the mountings with the workshop and settle the crew terms. Gao will lead the field survey. Bao will decide the medical work, and the drivers will have authority over their animals and moving loads. I will not send letters from my kitchen pretending I can judge a washed-out slope better than someone standing beside it. You can still write to me when you need more funds, provided there is an actual messenger and time for the answer. My daughter has requested that I practise being useful from a chair.

desert_p13_087.speaker: han_xun
desert_p13_087.text: I intend to surprise her by trying it.

desert_p13_088.speaker: narrator
desert_p13_088.text: The town's third story reached Yue at the rented room that night. According to the shopkeeper, the expedition had uncovered evidence that every map in Bitter Wells was false. Yue said several of them still led correctly to the bun seller. The shopkeeper considered that useful but insufficiently exciting. His daughter took the folded public warning from Yue and read it under the lamp. She asked whether the old blue well still had people beside it. Yue said the next enquiry hoped to find out. The girl folded the warning along its printed line.

desert_p13_089.speaker: narrator
desert_p13_089.text: Somewhere beyond the known ridge was a community that the town had almost turned into a number. Now it had become a destination. Before sleep Yue wrote the valley's historical name on a fresh page, leaving space beneath it. She added the gate identifiers and the sources that had supplied them. She did not draw a village she had never seen. The room's window stood open to warm night air; a neighbour's basin clinked below as he washed his feet.

desert_p13_090.speaker: narrator
desert_p13_090.text: Her own hands had healed enough to hold the brush comfortably, though she could still feel the cover's rough edge when she thought of the spill. The new road would not begin with that edge. It would begin with people asking whether the water moving north knew where it was going, and with a journey to see.
